channel.title: Clinical Research Chaos – open funding calls
channel.description: Open funding calls in clinical research, clinical engineering and rehabilitation, checked on the official text.

item.title: Immune Tolerance Network (UM1 Clinical Trial Required)
item.description: This notice of funding opportunity supports applications to continue the Immune Tolerance Network, aiming to develop tolerogenic therapies for immune-mediated disorders. Focus areas include allergic diseases and asthma, autoimmune diseases, and transplantation consequences. The network conducts clinical trials and integrated mechanistic studies. Eligible applicants include domestic and foreign institutions, such as non-profits, for-profits, higher education institutions, and government agencies. Programme: NIH – US National Institutes of Health. Eligible countries: Coming soon: published with the full call. Deadline: see the official call. Official call: https://www.grants.gov/search-results-detail/362946

item.title: MSCA Choose Europe for Science 2027
item.description: This call funds talent recruitment programmes proposed by academic and non-academic organisations to tackle brain drain and career precarity in Europe. Successful applicants implement co-funded programmes providing doctoral-degree holders with excellent research opportunities, training, and concrete long-term career prospects across two phases: an EU-funded phase and a beneficiary-funded phase covering salaries and management costs. Programme: Horizon Europe. Eligible countries: EU Member States and associated countries. Who can lead: Organisations holding a doctoral degree for the researchers they recruit, submitted by public or private research organisations, universities, and research cent. Deadline: 6 Apr 2027. Official call: https://ec.europa.eu/info/funding-tenders/opportunities/portal/screen/opportunities/topic-details/HORIZON-MSCA-2027-COFUND-02-01

item.title: MSCA Staff Exchanges 2027
item.description: The MSCA Staff Exchanges call funds international, inter-sectoral, and inter-disciplinary mobility of research and innovation staff through secondments. It aims to promote knowledge transfer, cooperation, and skills development between academic and non-academic organisations worldwide, including SMEs. Consortia involving independent legal entities can apply to implement a joint R&I project and foster long-term collaborations. Programme: Horizon Europe – HORIZON TMA MSCA Staff Exchanges. Eligible countries: EU Member States and associated countries. Who can lead: Organisations from academic and non-academic sectors constituting a partnership by seconding and/or hosting eligible staff members.. Deadline: 15 Apr 2027. Official call: https://ec.europa.eu/info/funding-tenders/opportunities/portal/screen/opportunities/topic-details/HORIZON-MSCA-2027-SE-01-01

item.title: MSCA Postdoctoral Fellowships 2027
item.description: This call provides postdoctoral fellowships to excellent researchers undertaking international mobility to enhance their research and transferable skills. Applications are made jointly by the researcher and a beneficiary in the academic or non-academic sector. European fellowships are open to researchers coming to or moving within Europe, while global fellowships involve an outgoing phase in a non-associated third country followed by a mandatory return phase to an EU Member State or Associated Country. Programme: Horizon Europe – HORIZON TMA MSCA Postdoctoral Fellowships. Eligible countries: EU Member States and associated countries. Who can lead: Postdoctoral researchers undertaking international mobility, applying jointly with a beneficiary organisation in the academic or non-academic sector.. Deadline: 8 Sep 2027. Official call: https://ec.europa.eu/info/funding-tenders/opportunities/portal/screen/opportunities/topic-details/HORIZON-MSCA-2027-PF-01-01

item.title: Improving equitable health outcomes and added value for and with cancer patients through health-economics research, health systems…
item.description: This call aims to improve equitable health outcomes and added value for people at risk of cancer and cancer patients by funding research in health economics, health systems, and epidemiological or outcomes analysis. Projects will develop methodologies, model cost-effectiveness, evaluate healthcare expenditures, and improve access to cancer control programmes. Eligible applicants include researchers, physicians, innovators, SMEs, and professionals collaborating in international consortia. Programme: Horizon Europe – HORIZON Research and Innovation Actions. Eligible countries: EU Member States and associated countries. Deadline: 16 Sep 2027. Official call: https://ec.europa.eu/info/funding-tenders/opportunities/portal/screen/opportunities/topic-details/HORIZON-MISS-2027-02-CANCER-04

item.title: Pre-commercial procurement of affordable solutions for healthcare systems in the areas of cancer technologies
item.description: This call supports pre-commercial procurement actions targeting consortia of procurers to develop and deploy affordable, innovative solutions in cancer technologies, medical devices, or medicines. Projects aim to stimulate market-ready solutions, improve clinical outcomes, and engage end-users. Consortia must validate innovations across at least five different EU Member States or Associated Countries. Public procurers and healthcare authorities form the consortia, while industrial actors and researchers can respond to tenders. Programme: Horizon Europe. Eligible countries: EU Member States and associated countries. Who can lead: Consortia of procurers with similar needs in the area of cancer-centred healthcare.. Deadline: 16 Sep 2027. Official call: https://ec.europa.eu/info/funding-tenders/opportunities/portal/screen/opportunities/topic-details/HORIZON-MISS-2027-02-CANCER-05

item.title: Phase 1 including first-in-human clinical trials to test biomarker-guided medicines or multi-modal treatment interventions for patients…
item.description: This funding call supports final preclinical validation and phase 1 clinical trials, including first-in-human studies, to evaluate biomarker-guided medicines or multi-modal treatments for rare and very rare cancers. Projects must involve patients and caregivers in defining endpoints and adhere to open science principles. Eligible applicants include researchers, physicians, innovators, startups, SMEs, and foundations forming international consortia involving entities from EU Member States and Associated Countries. Programme: Horizon Europe – HORIZON Research and Innovation Actions. Eligible countries: EU Member States and associated countries. Who can lead: Researchers, physicians, innovators, startup, spin-off and spin-out companies, SMEs, charities or foundations and other professionals from different disciplines. Deadline: 16 Sep 2027. Official call: https://ec.europa.eu/info/funding-tenders/opportunities/portal/screen/opportunities/topic-details/HORIZON-MISS-2027-02-CANCER-03

item.title: Development of Psychosocial Therapeutic and Preventive Interventions for Mental Disorders (R33 Clinical Trial Required)
item.description: This funding opportunity supports pilot research to develop and test innovative psychosocial therapeutic and preventive interventions for mental disorders. Using an experimental therapeutics approach, projects must replicate target engagement and test whether engaging the intervention target mediates changes in clinical outcomes. Eligible applicants include higher education institutions, nonprofits, for-profit organizations, governments, and non-domestic foreign entities. Programme: NIH – US National Institutes of Health. Eligible countries: Any country (non-US organisations eligible). Next deadline: 17 Feb 2027 (new applications). Official call: https://www.grants.gov/search-results-detail/357426

item.title: Early-Stage Development of Informatics Technologies for Cancer Research and Management (U01 Clinical Trial Optional)
item.description: This funding opportunity solicits applications for the early-stage development of enabling informatics technologies to improve the acquisition, management, analysis, and dissemination of data and knowledge across the cancer research continuum. Funded projects range from prototyping to initial tool development or significant modification of existing tools. Eligible applicants include domestic and foreign public and private organizations, including higher education institutions, nonprofits, for-profit businesses, and government entities. Programme: NIH – US National Institutes of Health. Eligible countries: Any country (non-US organisations eligible). Deadline: see the official call. Official call: https://www.grants.gov/search-results-detail/359892

item.title: Innovative Screening Approaches and Therapies for Screenable Disorders in Newborns (R01 - Clinical Trial Optional)
item.description: This funding opportunity encourages research to develop novel screening approaches and therapeutic interventions for conditions identified through newborn screening, or genetic conditions that could benefit from early detection. It funds basic, translational, and clinical studies, including optional clinical trials, aimed at improving health outcomes for infants with genetic or congenital disorders. Eligible applicants include higher education institutions, non-profits, for-profit organizations, local and state governments, and non-domestic foreign organizations. Programme: NIH – US National Institutes of Health. Eligible countries: Any country (non-US organisations eligible). Who can lead: Any individual(s) with the skills, knowledge, and resources necessary to carry out the proposed research as the Program Director(s)/Principal Investigator(s).. Next deadline: 5 Feb 2027 (new applications). Official call: https://www.grants.gov/search-results-detail/357485

item.title: Innovative Screening Approaches and Therapies for Screenable Disorders in Newborns (R21)
item.description: This funding opportunity encourages exploratory research focused on developing novel screening approaches and therapeutic interventions for conditions for which newborn screening has been implemented or for genetic conditions that could benefit from early detection. Supported by the NICHD, the R21 mechanism funds exploratory, novel studies or pilot data generation. Eligible applicants include higher education institutions, nonprofits, for-profit organizations, governments, and international organizations. Programme: NIH – US National Institutes of Health. Eligible countries: Any country (non-US organisations eligible). Who can lead: Any individual(s) with the skills, knowledge, and resources necessary to carry out the proposed research as the Program Director(s)/Principal Investigator(s).. Next deadline: 16 Feb 2027 (new applications). Official call: https://www.grants.gov/search-results-detail/357487

item.title: Early-Stage Innovative Technology Development for Basic and Clinical Cancer Research
item.description: The National Cancer Institute solicits grant applications proposing to develop innovative technologies for cancer research or clinical care. The emphasis is on early-stage projects proposing proof-of-concept and pilot studies to test the technical feasibility of proposed methods, tools, assays, platforms, or instruments. Eligible applicants include a wide range of organizations, including domestic and foreign institutions, non-profits, for-profits, and government agencies. Programme: Innovative Molecular Analysis Technologies (IMAT) Program. Eligible countries: Coming soon: published with the full call. Deadline: see the official call. Official call: https://www.grants.gov/search-results-detail/363169

item.title: Basic Research in Cancer Health Disparities (R21 Clinical Trial Not Allowed)
item.description: This funding opportunity encourages exploratory pilot and feasibility studies into the biological and genetic causes and mechanisms of cancer health disparities. It supports mechanistic studies of biological factors, development and testing of new methodologies or models, and secondary data analyses. Eligible applicants include higher education institutions, nonprofits, for-profit organizations, governments, and foreign organizations. Clinical trials are not allowed. Programme: NIH – US National Institutes of Health. Eligible countries: Any country (non-US organisations eligible). Next deadline: 16 Feb 2027 (new applications). Official call: https://www.grants.gov/search-results-detail/357193

item.title: Social Psychology
item.description: The Social Psychology Program at the U.S. National Science Foundation supports theoretically focused empirical investigations that advance fundamental social psychological explanations of human behavior, attitudes, and experience. Funding is provided for research and infrastructure proposals exploring how social forces shape human psychology. Eligible applicants include unrestricted entities, subject to program guidelines and scope priorities. Programme: U.S. National Science Foundation. Eligible countries: Not stated in the official text: check the call. Deadline: 15 Jan 2027. Official call: https://www.grants.gov/search-results-detail/344634

item.title: Healthy Tomorrows Partnership for Children Program (HTPCP)
item.description: The Healthy Tomorrows Partnership for Children Program aims to support community-based projects promoting access to preventive clinical and public health services for children. Funded projects focus on mental health, nutrition, health education, and physical activity to enhance childhood chronic disease prevention in rural and medically underserved areas. Various types of organizations, including nonprofits, educational institutions, and government entities, are generally eligible to apply. Programme: Health Resources and Services Administration. Eligible countries: Not stated in the official text: check the call. Deadline: 20 Jan 2027. Official call: https://www.grants.gov/search-results-detail/363533

item.title: Canine Cancer Immunotherapy Network (K9CIN; U01 Clinical Trial Not Allowed)
item.description: This funding opportunity supports the Canine Cancer Immunotherapy Network by funding a Network Coordinating Center and institutions conducting canine cancer immunotherapy clinical trials and correlative studies. The goal is to advance canine cancer treatments as a translational model for human therapies. Eligible applicants include domestic and foreign public and private organizations, including higher education institutions, nonprofits, businesses, and government agencies. Programme: NIH – US National Institutes of Health. Eligible countries: Coming soon: published with the full call. Deadline: see the official call. Official call: https://www.grants.gov/search-results-detail/361532

item.title: Swiss Government Excellence Scholarships
item.description: The Swiss Government Excellence Scholarships encourage international exchange and research cooperation by funding talented early career researchers and PhD candidates from abroad. The call supports full-time research fellowships and doctoral studies at Swiss higher education institutions or recognized research institutes. Eligible applicants must hold a Master's degree and secure an academic supervisor in Switzerland. Successful candidates receive a monthly stipend to cover basic living expenses. Programme: Swiss Government Excellence Scholarships. Eligible countries: Over 180 countries. Who can lead: Talented early career researchers from abroad who have completed their Master's degree and have a date of birth after 31 December 1991.. Deadline: 30 Nov 2026. Official call: https://servicios.colfuturo.org/apps/becasuiza/index.html

item.title: Maximizing the Scientific Value of Data Generated by the ECHO Program: NRSA Individual Postdoctoral Fellowship
item.description: This call funds Ruth L. Kirschstein National Research Service Award individual postdoctoral fellowships to advance research and training in high-priority child health areas. Postdoctoral fellows will analyze large longitudinal datasets from the Environmental Influences on Child Health Outcomes (ECHO) Cohort within the NICHD Data and Specimen Hub repository. Eligible applicants include domestic institutions and eligible individuals as specified by NIH guidelines. Programme: NIH – US National Institutes of Health. Eligible countries: United States only (foreign organisations not eligible). Who can lead: Postdoctoral fellows from relevant scientific disciplines.. Deadline: see the official call. Official call: https://www.grants.gov/search-results-detail/359150

item.title: McCune-Albright Syndrome and Fibrous Dysplasia Research Call 2026
item.description: This call funds innovative basic, translational, or clinical biomedical research programs focused on McCune-Albright syndrome and fibrous dysplasia of bone. Funded projects aim to clarify pathophysiological mechanisms, improve diagnosis and patient management, and develop innovative therapeutic strategies. Eligible lead applicants are principal investigators affiliated with public or foreign research organizations, academic institutions, or hospitals. The maximum grant is 100,000 euros for up to 24 months. Programme: Fondation Maladies Rares – Appels. Eligible countries: Not stated in the official text: check the call. Deadline: see the official call. Official call: https://fondation-maladiesrares.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/MASFD_AAP2026_call_text_vf.pdf

item.title: Pilot Testing, Implementation, and Evaluation of the Cervical, Breast and Colorectal Cancer Clinical Decision Support Tools
item.description: This funding opportunity from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention aims to pilot test, implement, and evaluate clinical decision support tools integrated into electronic health records to facilitate evidence-based screening and management for cervical, breast, and colorectal cancers. Component A focuses on cervical cancer tools within large health systems, while Component B focuses on breast and colorectal cancer tools. Eligible applicants include various US government, educational, and non-profit entities. Programme: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention - ERA. Eligible countries: Not stated in the official text: check the call. Deadline: 23 Mar 2027. Official call: https://www.grants.gov/search-results-detail/363309

item.title: Mentored Quantitative Research Development Award (Parent K25 Independent Clinical Trial Not Allowed)
item.description: This funding opportunity from the National Institutes of Health supports the Mentored Quantitative Research Career Development Award (K25). It attracts productive professionals with quantitative and engineering backgrounds to biomedical, behavioral, and clinical research. The award provides salary support and protected time for supervised study and research. Eligible applicants are domestic U.S. organizations, while foreign organizations are not eligible to apply. Independent clinical trials are not allowed. Programme: NIH – US National Institutes of Health. Eligible countries: United States only (foreign organisations not eligible). Who can lead: Quantitative scientists or engineers from postdoctoral to senior faculty level; U.S. citizen, non-citizen national, or permanent resident.. Next deadline: 12 Feb 2027 (new applications). Official call: https://www.grants.gov/search-results-detail/353710

item.title: Mentored Quantitative Research Development Award (Parent K25 Independent Clinical Trial Required)
item.description: This funding opportunity from the National Institutes of Health supports career development for quantitative scientists and engineers to apply their expertise to health and disease research. The K25 award provides protected time for supervised study and research. This specific notice requires candidates to serve as the lead investigator of an independent clinical trial, feasibility study, or ancillary clinical trial. Eligible applicants include domestic higher education, non-profit, and for-profit organizations. Programme: NIH – US National Institutes of Health. Eligible countries: United States only (foreign organisations not eligible). Who can lead: US citizen, non-citizen national, or permanent resident; holds an advanced quantitative degree; research-oriented investigator from postdoc to senior faculty.. Next deadline: 12 Feb 2027 (new applications). Official call: https://www.grants.gov/search-results-detail/353709

item.title: NIDCD Cooperative Agreement for Clinical Trials in Communication Disorders (U01 - Clinical Trial Required)
item.description: This funding opportunity supports investigator-initiated clinical trials focused on communication disorders such as hearing, balance, smell, taste, voice, speech, and language. The call funds cooperative agreements for clinical trials requiring FDA oversight, aiming to establish efficacy, or involving higher risks. Eligible applicants include domestic public and private higher education institutions, nonprofits, for-profit organizations, and local or tribal governments based in the United States. Programme: National Institute on Deafness and Other Communication Disorders (NIDCD). Eligible countries: United States only (foreign organisations not eligible). Who can lead: Any individual(s) with the skills, knowledge, and resources necessary to carry out the proposed research as the Program Director(s)/Principal Investigator(s).. Next deadline: 18 Feb 2027 (new applications). Official call: https://www.grants.gov/search-results-detail/358023

item.title: Leadership Education in Adolescent Health (LEAH)
item.description: The Leadership Education in Adolescent Health (LEAH) Program establishes adolescent and young adult health graduate training programs that aim to expand access to high quality, team-based health care. The program funds institutions of higher education and teaching hospitals to train health care professionals in addressing chronic disease prevention. Eligible applicants are limited to domestic non-profit private and public institutions of higher education. Programme: Health Resources and Services Administration. Eligible countries: United States only. Who can lead: Domestic non-profit private or public institutions of higher education and teaching hospitals. Individuals are not eligible applicants.. Deadline: 20 Jan 2027. Official call: https://www.grants.gov/search-results-detail/363410

item.title: BRAIN Initiative: Exploratory Research Opportunities Using Invasive Neural Recording and Stimulating Technologies in the Human Brain
item.description: This funding opportunity supports exploratory research projects from multidisciplinary teams to understand how single cells and neural networks in the human brain give rise to internal states and behaviors. Funded projects will establish feasibility and early-stage development using invasive neural recording and stimulation technologies during surgical procedures. Eligible applicants include domestic U.S. organizations such as institutions of higher education, non-profits, small businesses, and government entities. Programme: NIH – US National Institutes of Health. Eligible countries: United States only (foreign organisations not eligible). Who can lead: Refer to Section III. Eligibility Information in the NOFO for additional information on eligibility.. Deadline: see the official call. Official call: https://www.grants.gov/search-results-detail/359649

item.title: Supporting Talented Early Career Researchers in Genomics (R01 Clinical Trial Optional)
item.description: This funding opportunity supports exceptionally promising Early Stage Investigators pursuing innovative research in genomics relevant to the mission of the National Human Genome Research Institute. The scheme funds research projects, including optional clinical trials, to help early career researchers establish independent research programs. Eligible applicant organizations include domestic public and private higher education institutions, non-profits, and for-profit organizations. Programme: National Human Genome Research Institute (NHGRI). Eligible countries: United States only (foreign organisations not eligible). Who can lead: Must be an NIH-defined Early Stage Investigator, an independent researcher with a tenure-track or equivalent faculty appointment, with dedicated laboratory spac. Next deadline: 26 Feb 2027 (new applications). Official call: https://www.grants.gov/search-results-detail/357744

item.title: Toward Translation of Nanotechnology Cancer Interventions (TTNCI; R01 Clinical Trial Not Allowed)
item.description: This funding opportunity aims to enable the translation of nanotechnology-based cancer interventions relying on nanoparticle formulations and/or nano-devices, supporting advanced pre-clinical research for diagnostics and therapeutics. Eligible applicant organizations include higher education institutions, nonprofits, for-profit organizations, and various levels of government within the United States. Programme: NIH – US National Institutes of Health. Eligible countries: United States only (foreign organisations not eligible). Who can lead: Any individual(s) with the skills, knowledge, and resources necessary to carry out the proposed research as the Program Director(s)/Principal Investigator(s).. Next deadline: 16 Nov 2026 (new applications). Official call: https://www.grants.gov/search-results-detail/357748

item.title: Blueprint MedTech Translator (UG3/UH3 - Clinical Trial Optional)
item.description: This funding opportunity supports translational activities and clinical studies to accelerate the development of medical devices for disorders within the missions of participating NIH institutes and centers. Funding covers prototype implementation, non-clinical testing, design verification, and clinical studies. Eligible applicants include higher education institutions, non-profits, for-profit organizations, and foreign organizations. Programme: NIH – US National Institutes of Health. Eligible countries: Any country (non-US organisations eligible). Who can lead: Any individual(s) with the skills, knowledge, and resources necessary to carry out the proposed research as the Program Director(s)/Principal Investigator(s).. Next deadline: 28 Jan 2027 (new applications). Official call: https://www.grants.gov/search-results-detail/358823

item.title: Development of monoclonal antibodies to prevent and treat infections from Filo-, Nairo-, Phenui-, Picorna- and Toga viruses
item.description: This topic supports the development of prophylactic and therapeutic monoclonal antibody candidates targeting specific viruses, including Ebola, Marburg, Crimean-Congo Hemorrhagic Fever, Rift Valley Fever, Enterovirus D68, or Chikungunya. Funded activities include in-vitro characterisation, in-vivo animal testing, GMP-compliant batch production, and first-in-human clinical safety trials. Proposals should advance existing candidates, with the participation of start-ups, SMEs, and entities from endemic third countries encouraged. Programme: Horizon Europe – Cluster 1: Health. Eligible countries: EU Member States and associated countries. Deadline: 17 Feb 2027. Official call: https://ec.europa.eu/info/funding-tenders/opportunities/portal/screen/opportunities/topic-details/HORIZON-HLTH-2027-01-DISEASE-07

item.title: Integrating climate-related exposures into the human exposome and characterising its changes in response to climate change
item.description: This call supports research strengthening the use of the exposome approach to study global exposures and generate evidence on their health implications, focusing on integrating climate-related factors into exposome research. Funded activities include incorporating multiple climate exposures into exposomics studies, monitoring exposome changes resulting from climate pressures, advanced data analytics, and identifying exposome biomarkers. Collaborative multiscale and multidisciplinary projects involving social sciences and humanities can apply. Programme: Horizon Europe – Cluster 1: Health. Eligible countries: EU Member States and associated countries. Deadline: 17 Feb 2027. Official call: https://ec.europa.eu/info/funding-tenders/opportunities/portal/screen/opportunities/topic-details/HORIZON-HLTH-2027-01-ENVHLTH-02

item.title: Personalised approaches to reduce risks from Adverse Drug Reactions due to administration of multiple medications
item.description: This call supports research to reduce the incidence and severity of Adverse Drug Reactions (ADRs) resulting from multiple medications. Funded activities include leveraging pharmacogenomics, pharmacokinetics, and biomarkers for patient stratification, alongside integrating health technologies such as artificial intelligence and electronic health records into clinical practice. Proposals should also address clinical utility, guidelines, and regulatory implementation. Interdisciplinary consortia and clinical researchers, with the encouraged participation of SMEs and start-ups, can apply. Programme: Horizon Europe – Cluster 1: Health. Eligible countries: EU Member States and associated countries. Deadline: 17 Feb 2027. Official call: https://ec.europa.eu/info/funding-tenders/opportunities/portal/screen/opportunities/topic-details/HORIZON-HLTH-2027-01-CARE-02

item.title: Portable and versatile Point-of-care diagnostics
item.description: This topic supports the development, optimisation, and clinical validation of portable point-of-care (PoC) medical diagnostic devices adhering to the WHO REASSURED criteria. Proposals should address clear clinical needs, such as resource-limited settings, infectious disease discrimination, or non-communicable emergency care. Funded activities include device optimisation, comparative performance studies against the state of the art, and clinical studies fulfilling EU IVDR or MDR requirements. Applicants designing advanced diagnostic tools may apply. Programme: Horizon Europe – Cluster 1: Health. Eligible countries: EU Member States and associated countries. Stage 1 deadline: 17 Feb 2027 (two-stage call). Official call: https://ec.europa.eu/info/funding-tenders/opportunities/portal/screen/opportunities/topic-details/HORIZON-HLTH-2027-02-IND-02-two-stage

item.title: Development of novel small molecule antiviral therapeutics for pathogens with epidemic potential
item.description: This topic supports the development of novel or existing antiviral candidates targeting specific emerging and re-emerging viruses with epidemic potential, excluding antibodies. Funded activities include candidate discovery, structure-activity relationship optimization, in-vitro and in-vivo characterization, GMP manufacturing, and first-in-human clinical safety studies. Consortia are expected to engage with regulatory bodies, leverage research infrastructures, and encourage the participation of start-ups, SMEs, and entities from endemic third countries. Programme: Horizon Europe – Cluster 1: Health. Eligible countries: EU Member States and associated countries. Deadline: 17 Feb 2027. Official call: https://ec.europa.eu/info/funding-tenders/opportunities/portal/screen/opportunities/topic-details/HORIZON-HLTH-2027-01-DISEASE-05

item.title: BRAIN Initiative: Brain Behavior Quantification and Synchronization- Next Generation Sensor Technology Development (U01 Clinical Trial…
item.description: This funding opportunity supports the development of next-generation sensor technologies and bioelectronic devices that synchronize with brain recordings to model organismal and human behavior. It aims to foster multidisciplinary collaborations among engineers and behavioral scientists to create reliable, compact, real-time sensing tools. Eligible applicants include higher education institutions, non-profits, for-profit organizations, governments, and international foreign organizations. Programme: National Institutes of Health (NIH). Eligible countries: Any country (non-US organisations eligible). Who can lead: Any individual(s) with the skills, knowledge, and resources necessary to carry out the proposed research as the Program Director(s)/Principal Investigator(s).. Next deadline: 15 Jun 2027 (new applications). Official call: https://www.grants.gov/search-results-detail/356811

item.title: Bioengineering Partnerships with Industry (U01 Clinical Trial Optional)
item.description: This funding opportunity solicits applications from research partnerships formed by academic and industrial investigators to accelerate the development and adoption of promising bioengineering tools and technologies addressing important biomedical problems. The goal is to establish robust, well-characterized solutions fulfilling unmet needs within five to ten years. Eligible applicant organizations include higher education institutions, non-profits, for-profit organizations, and foreign entities. Programme: NIH – US National Institutes of Health. Eligible countries: Any country (non-US organisations eligible). Who can lead: Any individual(s) with the skills, knowledge, and resources necessary to carry out the proposed research as the Program Director(s)/Principal Investigator(s).. Next deadline: 27 Jan 2027 (new applications). Official call: https://www.grants.gov/search-results-detail/357019

item.title: Confirmatory Efficacy Clinical Trials of Non-Pharmacological and Pharmacological Interventions for Mental Disorders
item.description: This funding opportunity supports confirmatory efficacy testing of non-pharmacological and, under certain conditions, pharmacological preventive and therapeutic interventions for mental disorders in adults and children. Projects must employ an experimental therapeutics approach to examine mechanisms of action, target engagement, and clinical outcomes. Eligible applicants include higher education institutions, non-profits, for-profit organizations, governments, and foreign organizations. Programme: NIH – US National Institutes of Health. Eligible countries: Any country (non-US organisations eligible). Who can lead: Any individual(s) with the skills, knowledge, and resources necessary to carry out the proposed research as the PD/PI is invited to work with their organization. Next deadline: 17 Feb 2027 (new applications). Official call: https://www.grants.gov/search-results-detail/357423

item.title: Early Stage Testing of Pharmacologic or Neuromodulatory Device-based Interventions for the Treatment of Mental Disorders
item.description: This funding opportunity supports early-stage clinical trial applications evaluating novel pharmacologic or neuromodulatory device-based interventions for mental disorders. The aim is to test target engagement and mechanism of action alongside clinical or functional outcomes in pediatric, adult, and geriatric populations. Eligible applicants include higher education institutions, non-profits, for-profit organizations, governments, and foreign entities. Programme: NIH – US National Institutes of Health. Eligible countries: Any country (non-US organisations eligible). Who can lead: Any individual(s) with the skills, knowledge, and resources necessary to carry out the proposed research as the Program Director(s)/Principal Investigator(s).. Next deadline: 17 Feb 2027 (new applications). Official call: https://www.grants.gov/search-results-detail/357430

item.title: Full-Scale Hybrid Effectiveness-Implementation Trials for Mental Health Interventions
item.description: This funding opportunity supports well-powered clinical trials to evaluate the effectiveness and implementation of optimized mental health prevention and treatment interventions in real-world settings. Projects must examine implementation challenges, clinical impact, and at least one mechanism of action. Eligible applicants include higher education institutions, nonprofits, for-profit organizations, local and state governments, tribal governments, and foreign organizations. Programme: NIH – US National Institutes of Health. Eligible countries: Any country (non-US organisations eligible). Who can lead: Any individual(s) with the skills, knowledge, and resources necessary to carry out the proposed research as the Program Director(s)/Principal Investigator(s).. Next deadline: 17 Feb 2027 (new applications). Official call: https://www.grants.gov/search-results-detail/357421

item.title: Pilot Hybrid Effectiveness-Implementation Trials for Mental Health Interventions
item.description: This funding opportunity supports pilot hybrid effectiveness-implementation research to optimize preventive and therapeutic mental health interventions and related implementation strategies in accessible settings such as routine care, schools, communities, or online platforms. Proposed projects must test intervention effectiveness, implementation factors, and mechanisms of action. Eligible applicants include higher education institutions, non-profits, for-profit organizations, governments, and foreign organizations. Clinical trials are required. Programme: NIH – US National Institutes of Health. Eligible countries: Any country (non-US organisations eligible). Who can lead: Any individual(s) with the skills, knowledge, and resources necessary to carry out the proposed research as the Program Director(s)/Principal Investigator(s).. Next deadline: 17 Feb 2027 (new applications). Official call: https://www.grants.gov/search-results-detail/357422

item.title: Effectiveness Trials to Test Mental Health System Interventions (R61/R33 Clinical Trial Required)
item.description: This funding opportunity supports milestone-driven feasibility and infrastructure development research followed by a well-powered clinical trial to test the effectiveness of system interventions or strategies. The aim is to improve the organization, delivery, coordination, and outcomes of mental health care. Funded interdisciplinary centers will conduct high-impact, practice-based research to rapidly develop, test, and refine novel interventions that improve mental health care access, quality, and outcomes. Eligible applicants include higher education institutions, nonprofits, for-profit organizations, governments, and tribal organizations. Programme: NIH – US National Institutes of Health. Eligible countries: Coming soon: published with the full call. Deadline: see the official call. Official call: https://www.grants.gov/search-results-detail/361521

item.title: Childhood Asthma in Urban Settings Clinical Research Network
item.description: This funding opportunity supports the Childhood Asthma in Urban Settings Clinical Research Network to advance multi-site clinical studies and trials on asthma prevention and treatment in economically disadvantaged pediatric populations. Funded research includes developing prevention strategies, testing new treatment targets, and identifying disease endotypes using systems biology. Eligible applicants include higher education institutions, nonprofits, small businesses, for-profit organizations, tribal and local governments, and federal agencies. Programme: Childhood Asthma in Urban Settings Clinical Research Network (CAUSE). Eligible countries: Coming soon: published with the full call. Deadline: see the official call. Official call: https://www.grants.gov/search-results-detail/362950

item.title: First in Human and Early Stage Clinical Trials of Novel Investigational Drugs or Neuromodulatory Device-based Interventions
item.description: This funding opportunity supports milestone-driven early stage clinical trials, including first-in-human, Phase Ib, Phase II/PoC, and early feasibility studies for novel investigational drugs or neuromodulatory devices addressing psychiatric disorders. The goal is to de-risk these interventions to attract further clinical development funding. Eligible applicants include higher education institutions, non-profits, for-profit organizations, and government entities based in the United States. Programme: NIH – US National Institutes of Health. Eligible countries: United States only (foreign organisations not eligible). Who can lead: Any individual(s) with the skills, knowledge, and resources necessary to carry out the proposed research as the Program Director(s)/Principal Investigator(s).. Next deadline: 17 Feb 2027 (new applications). Official call: https://www.grants.gov/search-results-detail/357424

item.title: Catalyze Product Definition Medical Device prototype design/testing and disease target identification and assay development
item.description: This funding call provides early stage translational support to develop and test device prototype designs, identify diagnostic disease targets, develop associated assays, and build research tools for treating heart, lung, blood, and sleep diseases and disorders. Structured as an R61/R33 phased award, it funds prototype design and initial testing in the first phase, followed by further optimization and validation. Eligible applicants include domestic higher education institutions, non-profits, for-profit organizations, and governments. Programme: NIH – US National Institutes of Health. Eligible countries: United States only (foreign organisations not eligible). Who can lead: Any individual(s) with the skills, knowledge, and resources necessary to carry out the proposed research as the Program Director(s)/Principal Investigator(s).. Next deadline: 11 Feb 2027 (new applications). Official call: https://www.grants.gov/search-results-detail/357339

item.title: Catalyze: Product Definition Medical Device Prototype Optimization (R33 - Clinical Trial Not Allowed)
item.description: This National Institutes of Health funding opportunity provides early-stage translational support for prototype testing, design modification, diagnostic assay development, and research tools targeting heart, lung, blood, and sleep diseases. The goal is to advance innovations toward preclinical testing or external development. Eligible applicants include domestic higher education institutions, non-profits, for-profit organizations, and governments. Foreign organizations are ineligible. Programme: NIH – US National Institutes of Health. Eligible countries: United States only (foreign organisations not eligible). Who can lead: Any individual(s) with the skills, knowledge, and resources necessary to carry out the proposed research as the Program Director(s)/Principal Investigator(s).. Next deadline: 11 Feb 2027 (new applications). Official call: https://www.grants.gov/search-results-detail/357340

item.title: NIDCR Behavioral and Social Intervention Clinical Trial Planning and Implementation Cooperative Agreement
item.description: This funding opportunity provides support for the planning and implementation of behavioral and biopsychosocial intervention studies relevant to dental, oral, and craniofacial health that meet the NIH definition of a clinical trial. It uses a phased cooperative agreement supporting a milestone-driven planning phase followed by a clinical trial implementation phase. Eligible applicants include higher education institutions, nonprofits, for-profit organizations, and local or state governments based in the United States. Programme: NIH – US National Institutes of Health. Eligible countries: United States only (foreign organisations not eligible). Who can lead: Any individual(s) with the skills, knowledge, and resources necessary to carry out the proposed research as the Program Director(s)/Principal Investigator(s).. Next deadline: 8 Feb 2027 (new applications). Official call: https://www.grants.gov/search-results-detail/357462

item.title: NIDCR Drug, Biologic, Device and/or Procedure Intervention Clinical Trial Planning and Implementation Cooperative Agreement
item.description: This funding opportunity supports phased, milestone-driven cooperative agreement applications to plan and implement clinical trials within the NIDCR mission. It funds studies testing drugs, biologics, devices, or procedures to improve dental, oral, or craniofacial health through a one-year UG3 planning phase and up to five years of UH3 implementation. Eligible applicants include higher education institutions, nonprofits, for-profit organizations, and governments based in the United States. Programme: NIH – US National Institutes of Health. Eligible countries: United States only (foreign organisations not eligible). Who can lead: Any individual(s) with the skills, knowledge, and resources necessary to carry out the proposed research as the Program Director(s)/Principal Investigator(s).. Next deadline: 8 Feb 2027 (new applications). Official call: https://www.grants.gov/search-results-detail/356815

item.title: Advancing Healthcare for Older Adults from Populations that Experience Health Disparities
item.description: This funding opportunity aims to advance innovative multi-level healthcare research for older adults from populations experiencing health disparities. It supports research to improve screening and clinical care guidelines, enhance shared decision-making between clinicians, patients, and caregivers, and identify effective care coordination strategies. Eligible applicants include higher education institutions, nonprofits, for-profit organizations, local and state governments, and tribal governments based in the United States. Programme: NIH – US National Institutes of Health. Eligible countries: United States only (foreign organisations not eligible). Who can lead: Any individual(s) with the skills, knowledge, and resources necessary to carry out the proposed research as the Program Director(s)/Principal Investigator(s).. Next deadline: 5 Feb 2027 (new applications). Official call: https://www.grants.gov/search-results-detail/356236

item.title: Ruth L. Kirschstein National Research Service Award (NRSA) Institutional Research Training Grant (Parent T32)
item.description: The National Institutes of Health awards Institutional Research Training Grants (T32) to eligible domestic institutions to develop or enhance predoctoral and postdoctoral research training. The goal is to ensure a highly trained biomedical, behavioral, and clinical research workforce. Programs must incorporate engaging didactic, research, and career development elements. Only domestic U.S. institutions may apply, and foreign entities or foreign components are explicitly excluded from participating as applicants. Programme: NIH – US National Institutes of Health. Eligible countries: United States only (foreign organisations not eligible). Who can lead: Any individual(s) with the skills, knowledge, and resources necessary to carry out the proposed research training program as the Training Program Director/PI.. Next deadline: 25 Jan 2027 (new applications). Official call: https://www.grants.gov/search-results-detail/357140

item.title: Clinical Trial Readiness for Rare Diseases, Disorders, and Syndromes
item.description: This call invites researchers to submit applications for clinical projects addressing critical needs for clinical trial readiness in rare diseases. It aims to facilitate rare diseases research by enabling the movement of candidate therapeutics or diagnostics toward clinical trials through the development of rigorous biomarkers, clinical outcome assessment measures, or natural history studies. Eligible applicants include various U.S. institutional types. Clinical trials are not allowed. Programme: NIH – US National Institutes of Health. Eligible countries: United States only (foreign organisations not eligible). Who can lead: Any individual(s) with the skills, knowledge, and resources necessary to carry out the proposed research as the Program Director(s)/Principal Investigator(s).. Next deadline: 17 Feb 2027 (new applications). Official call: https://www.grants.gov/search-results-detail/359645

item.title: Transformative Non-Invasive/Minimally Invasive Technologies for Imaging the Olfactory System Across Scales (R01 CT Optional)
item.description: This funding opportunity from the National Institutes of Health supports the development and adaptation of transformative in vivo high-resolution, high-specificity imaging technologies for the human olfactory system across scales. Projects must leverage advanced non-invasive or minimally invasive imaging to visualize peripheral and central olfactory targets. Multidisciplinary teams combining expertise in olfaction, biomedical imaging, biochemistry, bioengineering, and biophysics are encouraged. Non-U.S. entities and foreign components are not eligible to apply. Programme: NIH – US National Institutes of Health. Eligible countries: United States only (foreign organisations not eligible). Deadline: see the official call. Official call: https://www.grants.gov/search-results-detail/359696

item.title: MS Australia Grant Application Portal
item.description: MS Australia offers a range of project grants, fellowships, scholarships, and travel awards to support research relevant to multiple sclerosis. The funding aims to advance knowledge, treatment, or management of MS. Eligible applicants must be Australian or New Zealand citizens or permanent residents. Programme: MS Australia Grant Program. Eligible countries: Australia and New Zealand only. Who can lead: Australian or New Zealand citizen or permanent resident.. Deadline: see the official call. Official call: https://grants.msaustralia.org.au/

item.title: Translational Neural Devices (R61/R33 - Clinical Trial Optional)
item.description: This National Institutes of Health funding opportunity encourages researchers to pursue translational activities and small clinical studies to advance the development of low-risk therapeutic and diagnostic devices for disorders affecting the nervous or neuromuscular systems. Funded activities include clinical prototype implementation, non-clinical safety testing, design verification, and subsequent small clinical studies. Eligible applicants include domestic and foreign higher education institutions, nonprofits, for-profit organizations, and governments. Programme: NIH – US National Institutes of Health. Eligible countries: Any country (non-US organisations eligible). Who can lead: Any individual(s) with the skills, knowledge, and resources necessary to carry out the proposed research as the Program Director(s)/Principal Investigator(s).. Next deadline: 28 Jan 2027 (new applications). Official call: https://www.grants.gov/search-results-detail/356903

item.title: Multimodal AI to Accelerate Precision Medicine for Type 1 Diabetes (U01- Clinical Trials Not Allowed)
item.description: This funding opportunity forecast supports milestone-driven research combining multimodal human pancreas and clinical datasets to understand how biological processes interact in type 1 diabetes (T1D). The initiative funds the development and testing of multimodal artificial intelligence models, AI-enabled research workflows, data integration methods, and privacy-preserving synthetic datasets. Eligible applicants include higher education institutions, nonprofits, for-profit organizations, state and local governments, and non-domestic (foreign) entities. Clinical trials are not allowed. Programme: NIH – US National Institutes of Health. Eligible countries: Coming soon: published with the full call. Deadline: see the official call. Official call: https://www.grants.gov/search-results-detail/363678

item.title: Valorising Horizon project results via innovation ecosystems
item.description: This call aims to bridge the structural gap between Horizon research outcomes and market-oriented support mechanisms. It funds consortia of knowledge intermediaries to scout promising innovations, launch competitive calls for third-party financial support, and provide expert mentorship, validation, and valorisation services. Applicants must be entities forming consortia acting as knowledge intermediaries within innovation ecosystems. Programme: Horizon Europe. Eligible countries: EU Member States and associated countries. Deadline: 16 Feb 2027. Official call: https://ec.europa.eu/info/funding-tenders/opportunities/portal/screen/opportunities/topic-details/HORIZON-BRIDGING-2027-06-02

item.title: Multi-Site Investigator-Initiated Clinical Trials (Collaborative UG3/UH3 Clinical Trial Required)
item.description: This upcoming NIH funding opportunity will solicit applications to develop and implement investigator-initiated multi-site clinical trials, including efficacy, effectiveness, pragmatic, or implementation research, as well as complex virtual trials. The scheme supports projects through a bi-phasic mechanism consisting of a start-up phase of up to two years and a trial implementation phase of up to five years. Higher education institutions, non-profits, for-profit businesses, and non-domestic foreign entities will be eligible to apply. Programme: NIH – US National Institutes of Health. Eligible countries: Coming soon: published with the full call. Deadline: see the official call. Official call: https://www.grants.gov/search-results-detail/363025

item.title: Development of monoclonal antibodies to prevent and treat infections from Flaviviruses
item.description: This call aims to support the development of prophylactic and therapeutic monoclonal antibody candidates targeting specific Flaviviruses such as Dengue, Tick-borne Encephalitis, Japanese Encephalitis, West Nile Fever, Yellow Fever, and Zika. Funded activities include in-vitro and in-vivo testing, GMP batch production, and first-in-human clinical safety studies. Eligible applicants include research entities, universities, start-ups, and SMEs from EU member states and associated countries forming consortia. Programme: Horizon Europe – Cluster 1: Health. Eligible countries: EU Member States and associated countries. Deadline: 17 Feb 2027. Official call: https://ec.europa.eu/info/funding-tenders/opportunities/portal/screen/opportunities/topic-details/HORIZON-HLTH-2027-01-DISEASE-06

item.title: Advanced Rehabilitation Research Training (ARRT) Program - Community Living and Participation
item.description: This opportunity under the Advanced Rehabilitation Research Training (ARRT) Program aims to provide advanced multidisciplinary research training to individuals with doctorates or similar advanced degrees, including researchers with disabilities. Funded projects must focus on community living and participation outcomes for people with disabilities. A single grant with a 36-month project period will be awarded. Public, state-controlled, and private institutions of higher education are eligible to apply; foreign entities are excluded. Programme: Advanced Rehabilitation Research Training (ARRT) Program. Eligible countries: United States only. Deadline: 7 Dec 2026. Official call: https://www.grants.gov/search-results-detail/363963

item.title: Cooperative Research Agreements Related to the World Trade Center Health Program (U01)
item.description: The National Institute for Occupational Safety and Health (NIOSH) seeks research project applications to optimize member care, diagnose and treat health conditions related to the September 11, 2001 terrorist attacks, and expand scientific knowledge on physical and mental health impacts. Eligible applicants include domestic public and private non-profit organizations, higher education institutions, local and state governments, and small businesses. Programme: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention - ERA. Eligible countries: United States only (foreign organisations not eligible). Who can lead: Anyone who has the skills, knowledge, and resources needed to carry out the proposed research as a project director or principal investigator (PD/PI).. Next deadline: 8 Dec 2026 (new applications). Official call: https://www.grants.gov/search-results-detail/356163

item.title: NHLBI Early Phase Clinical Trials for Therapeutics and/or Diagnostics for HLBS Disorders (R61/R33 Clinical Trial Required)
item.description: This funding opportunity supports investigator-initiated, Phase I clinical trials and final stage preclinical activities for diagnostic and therapeutic interventions targeting heart, lung, blood, and sleep disorders. Funded projects will utilize a bi-phasic, milestone-driven R61/R33 mechanism to support both start-up and execution phases. Eligible applicants include higher education institutions, non-profits, for-profit organizations, and government entities based in the United States and its territories. Programme: National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute (NHLBI). Eligible countries: United States only (foreign organisations not eligible). Who can lead: Any individual(s) with the skills, knowledge, and resources necessary to carry out the proposed research as the Program Director(s)/Principal Investigator(s).. Next deadline: 3 Feb 2027 (new applications). Official call: https://www.grants.gov/search-results-detail/357543
